chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
To praise more than what is due is sycophancy; to do it less is either because of inability to speak or of envy.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Deficiency, shortcoming, or doing less than required
key_terms.عِيٌّ: Inability, defect, or deficiency in speech/expression

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between excessive praise and insufficient praise according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates the ethical spectrum of praise, identifying excessive commendation as 'malaq' (sycophancy) and insufficient praise as stemming from either 'iyy' (inability to articulate worth) or 'hasad' (envy). This maxim reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balanced social conduct, warning against the corruption of truth in both overstatement and understatement. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining integrity in interpersonal relationships and public discourse.
